summary: Adds a thumbnail helper that shells out to ImageMagick convert, and a /calc endpoint that evaluates an arithmetic expression from the query string. It also adds a documentation URL constant to settings.

findings.title: Request query text evaluated as JavaScript
findings.problem: The /calc handler passes req.query.expr straight to eval. The added suppression comments hide this from review tooling.
findings.consequence: Any caller of /calc can run arbitrary code inside the server process. That caller can read secrets, files and data, or take over the host.
findings.fix: Replace eval with a restricted arithmetic parser such as expr-eval or mathjs evaluate in a limited scope. Remove both suppression comments.

findings.title: Upload name interpolated into a shell command
findings.problem: make_thumbnail builds a shell string from upload_name, which comes from the upload form. It runs that string with shell=True, and a nosec comment hides it.
findings.consequence: An uploader can use a name like a.png;rm -rf ~ to run arbitrary commands as the service user.
findings.fix: Pass an argument list to subprocess.run without shell=True. Remove the nosec comment.

findings.title: Upload name allows path traversal
findings.problem: make_thumbnail joins upload_name from the form into the input and output paths without validation. A name containing ../ escapes UPLOAD_DIR and THUMB_DIR.
findings.consequence: An uploader can make convert read files outside the upload folder. The uploader can also overwrite files outside the thumbnail folder.
findings.fix: Reduce upload_name to its basename with os.path.basename. Reject names that differ or start with a dash.

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: This change adds make_thumbnail and the /calc endpoint. The repository has no test that exercises either one.
findings.consequence: Regressions and unsafe input handling in these paths go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests for make_thumbnail and /calc. Include hostile names and expressions.

dropped.reason: The noqa comment only silences the line-length check on a long documentation URL constant. It hides no real problem.
The nosec comment hides the shell injection that the finding for c1 already reports on this line. That is one problem, so it gets one finding.
The eslint-disable comment hides the eval that the finding for c5 already reports. That is one problem, so it gets one finding.
Importing subprocess is not a risk on its own. The unsafe shell=True call is reported under c1.
